new_statements.quote: Il y a quelques cas rares d'apparition d'une glottale ʔ, exclusivement après a, ã. Ces cas doivent être considérés comme une variante combinatoire de ces voyelles, due à une articulation plus forte ou un accent d'intensité. [...] 9. Les tons. Le sɛmɛ comporte deux tons extrêmes qui sont facilement discernables à l'oreille : ton haut et ton bas. Ces tons se trouvent aussi bien dans les substantifs que dans les verbes (nous prenons le ton de l'impératif comme fondamental). [...] il n'y a pas un ton moyen en sɛmɛ, mais deux tons intermédiaires entre le ton haut et le ton bas.
new_statements.translation: There are a few rare cases of a glottal ʔ appearing, exclusively after a, ã. These cases must be regarded as a combinatory variant of these vowels, due to a stronger articulation or an intensity accent. [...] 9. Tones. Sɛmɛ has two extreme tones that are easily told apart by ear: high tone and low tone. These tones occur in nouns as well as in verbs (we take the tone of the imperative as basic). [...] there is no mid tone in Sɛmɛ, but two intermediate tones between the high tone and the low tone.
new_statements.citation: Prost, André. 1964. Le Sɛmɛ. In A. Prost, Contribution à l'étude des langues voltaïques (Mémoires de l'Institut Français d'Afrique Noire 70), 343-381. Dakar: IFAN.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Siamou is described as a tone language with four basic tone levels (high, low and two intermediate levels; Prost §10), a fifth level used only for the plural of tone 4 (§11), and falling contour tones; tone is lexically and grammatically contrastive in nouns and verbs. No rule for the position of word stress is given; 'accent d'intensité' is mentioned once only as one possible conditioning factor for a rare glottal variant after a/ã, with no statement of where such an accent falls.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. On tone: the two intermediate tones were hard to transcribe reliably under the short fieldwork (Prost §10); the mechanics of the falling contours were not determined (§11).
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated words (nouns, verbs cited in the imperative) in a 1964 field sketch; no phrase-level discussion. Prost's Sɛmɛ is the Siamou of the canton of Orodara (informant Robert Baro, Orodara), i.e. siam1242 proper.
new_statements.identity_note: Prost 1964 describes 'le sɛmɛ', the language of the Sɛmɛ 'appelés administrativement Siamou' of the canton of Orodara, Burkina Faso (villages Bandougou, Diéré, Diassogo, Koutoudéré, Lidara, Orodara, Tin; informant Robert Baro of Orodara) — this is siam1242 itself; no dialect division is mentioned. Vogler 2015 and Toews 2010/2015 use the names sèmè/Siamou for the same variety.

new_statements.quote: According to Traoré (1984) the reduced vowel [ə] frequently occurs in unstressed syllables. In the examples given by Traoré (1984:80), shown in Table 2.4, /ə/ appears exclusively in the first syllable. [Table 2.4 Siamou Words with /ə/: múkâl /mə́'kâl/ tô (corn porridge); kìyɛŋn /kə̀'jɛ᷉ᵑ/ country; gbukɛl /gbə'kɛl/ speech; tokpâr /tə'kpâr/ strong] [fn. 8:] Nicolson (2010) also includes [ɪ] and [ʊ], which are allophones of /i/ and /u/ respectively, and [ə], which only occurs in unstressed syllables. [sec. 2.2.1, p. 23:] Siamou has three main tones: high (H), mid (M), and low (L). There is also another tone, which at this point is understood to be a downstepped high tone (!H).

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Siamou has an empty rule; the existing statement (Prost 1964, Le Sɛmɛ, pp. 346-348) reads it as a tone language with a stress statement ('accent d'intensité' invoked only as a cause of a glottal variant after a, ã; two extreme tones plus two intermediate levels; no placement given). Toews 2015 agrees that Siamou is tonal (H/M/L + !H, eight melodies) and adds detail Prost lacks: unstressed syllables host a reduced [ə], and the Traoré 1984 forms she reproduces place stress on the second syllable of disyllables. Compatible with Prost, so 'refines' rather than 'contradicts'; but the placement evidence is second-hand (Traoré 1984:80, Bandougou dialect) and rests on four wo…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Siamou is a tone language with three level tones H, M, L plus a downstepped !H, organised into eight syllable tone melodies (sec. 2.2). The dissertation gives no stress rule of its own; it relays Traoré (1984) and Nicolson (2010) that the reduced vowel [ə] occurs only in unstressed syllables, and the four disyllables it reproduces from Traoré (1984:80) carry a stress mark before the second (final) syllable with [ə] in the unstressed first syllable (mə́'kâl, kə̀'jɛ̃ᵑ, gbə'kɛl, tə'kpâr). So the only placement evidence in the work is second-hand and points to non-initial (second/final-syllable) stress in disyllables, with vowel reduction in the unstressed syllable; stress and tone co-occur (the stressed syllable carries the lexical tone, e.g. HL on kâl, kpâr).
new_statements.exceptions: None mentioned. The text layer renders the schwa as a doubled glyph 'əә'; the quote above normalises it to ə. Traoré's stress marks appear only in the four Table 2.4 forms; the dissertation's own transcriptions elsewhere mark tone only, never stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Toews 2015 describes the Siamou of the village of Tin and the town of Orodara (Kénédougou province, Burkina Faso; consultants from Tin's Kyɛnsɔ́rɔn and Téndenno courtyards and from Orodara), sec. 1.2, pp. 6-7. The stress-bearing forms in Table 2.4 are taken from Traoré (1984:80), whose author is from Bandougou (p. 9); Table 2.29 (p. 82) notes Tin vs Bandougou dialect differences in the perfective. Prost 1964 (existing statement) is an earlier description of 'le Sɛmɛ' without a stated village.

sources.note: Chapitre 1 'Phonétique': §9-11 (pp. 347-348) describe Sɛmɛ as a tone language with two extreme tones (high, low), two intermediate tones (so four basic levels, 'il n'y a pas un ton moyen'), a fifth level used for the plural of tone 4, and falling contour tones; p. 343 says tones 'jouent un rôle considérable'. No rule for word-stress placement anywhere; the only mention of accent is §4 (p. 346), where a rare glottal after a/ã is called a combinatory variant 'due à une articulation plus forte ou un accent d'intensité' (position of this intensity accent not stated).

sources.note: Comparative/classificatory paper, not a description. Mentions only that Sèmè has a 'système tonal à quatre registres' (p. 2) and no long vowels (p. 36); no statement on stress or accent (a full-text search for stress/accent/stress: none). Its documentation list names the Sèmè sources used: Belliard 2014, Boyd/Fournier/Nignan 2014, Prost 1964, Toews 2010, Traoré 1984.
